notes.irrbbEveSensitivityPct: TD Table 31 "Structural Interest Rate Sensitivity Measures" (Q3 2024 Report to Shareholders, disclosed quarterly). notes.irrbbNiiSensitivityPct: Same Table 31: +100bp parallel increase → 12-month NII impact +$785mm (total) ÷ Net Tier 1 Capital $88,898mm = 0.88%. Recorded at the +100bp shock (same direction as the EVE figure) for consistency with TD's own Q4 disclosure; a derived ratio, not published by TD.

notes.irrbbEveSensitivityPct: TD discloses only a +/-100bps parallel shock EVE/NII sensitivity (Table 45, 'Structural Interest Rate Sensitivity Measures'), not the full six-scenario Basel/OSFI IRRBB template — confirmed absent from the FY2024 Annual Report, FY2025 Annual Report, and Q4 2025 Pillar 3 Supplemental Regulatory Disclosure. Most adverse of the two disclosed scenarios is the +100bps parallel increase: EVE impact -$2,489mm. Tier 1 Capital as at Oct 31, 2024 was $93,248mm (Capital Position Basel III (CC1) table, Q4 2025 Supplemental Regulatory Disclosure, prior-period comparative column) → -2489/93248 = -2.67%. notes.irrbbNiiSensitivityPct: Same Table 45: +100bps parallel increase → NII impact +$720mm / Tier 1 Capital $93,248mm = 0.77%. The -100bps decrease scenario gave NII -$983mm (-1.05% of T1), a larger-magnitude (more adverse) NII impact than the increase scenario.

irrbbDisclosureNote: TD discloses IRRBB every quarter in its Report to Shareholders MD&A under the 'Structural Interest Rate Sensitivity Measures' table (Table 31 in the interim reports; Table 45 in the year-end Annual Report). It does not use the standardized six-scenario Basel/OSFI IRRBB1 template (parallel up, parallel down, steepener, flattener, short rate up, short rate down) — that template could not be found in TD's quarterly Reports to Shareholders, the FY2024/FY2025 Annual Reports, or the Q4 2025 Pillar 3 Supplemental Regulatory Disclosure, despite TD being a G-SIB/D-SIB subject to OSFI's Pillar 3 guideline. Instead, TD shows both Economic Value of Shareholders' Equity (EVE) Sensitivity and Net Interest Income (NII) Sensitivity for a single prescribed shock: an immediate and sustained +/-100 basis point parallel shift, before-tax. Effective July 31, 2025, TD began splitting the two sensitivity measures by currency (Canadian dollar vs. U.S. dollar) in addition to the total. Both measures explicitly exclude exposures from the Wholesale Banking segment. TD does not itself express either sensitivity as a percentage of any capital base — the %-of-Tier-1 figures in this dataset were computed by dividing TD's disclosed dollar sensitivity by TD's Net Tier 1 Capital from the same quarter's Basel III Capital Position (CC1) table.
